acceptance: A31 — INT-07 public IPFS mirror with viewer fallback, INT-08 private swarm isolation

verdict.INT-07: FAIL (measured) — the mirror, the toggle, real gateway playback, the privacy fence and the kill switch all hold; three delivery/observability clauses do not
verdict.INT-08: PASS — replication is intra-swarm only, the outsider is refused at the security handshake, and no private CID reaches any API payload

topology.core: two processes from one binary — VIDRA_ROLE=api on 127.0.0.1:8088, VIDRA_ROLE=worker (no listener); schema 142, dirty=false; STORAGE_BACKEND=local; native PostgreSQL 16 and Redis, no Docker
topology.frontend: next build WITH NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3210, node .next/standalone/server.js on :3211 behind a pipe-only one-origin proxy on :3210
topology.kubo: 0.40.1 (Homebrew), four repos under the scratch dir with distinct IPFS_PATH and ports

public.role: the instance's public mirror + its gateway
public.daemon_line: Swarm not listening, running in offline mode.

private_p1.flags: LIBP2P_FORCE_PNET=1 + swarm.key, AutoConf.Enabled=false, Routing.Type=none, bootstrap rm --all
private_p1.daemon_line: Swarm is limited to private network of peers with the swarm key

private_p2.daemon_line: Swarm is limited to private network of peers with the swarm key

topology.irreversibility: A real public IPFS publication is IRREVERSIBLE: once a CID is announced, any peer that fetched it may keep and re-serve it, and unpinning removes only this instance's copy. This lab therefore NEVER published to the public network. The public node ran with --offline (swarm not listening, no DHT, no bitswap) and the private pair ran under LIBP2P_FORCE_PNET with a lab-generated swarm key and no bootstrap peers. Every CID recorded here exists only on this machine.

SC1_mirror_and_playback.verdict: PASS for the eligible path, FAIL for delete (fixed on vidra-core#218)
SC1_mirror_and_playback.detail_object_is_really_sent: GET /videos/{id} returned ipfs.original_cid, ipfs.hls_cid and ipfs.gateway_url for a public+published video — the mocked-green defect recorded under 'Mocked tests hide dead features' is fixed; the watch toggle gates on that object, not on the card-only ipfs_pinned flag
SC1_mirror_and_playback.privacy_fence_readback: private and unlisted uploads produced ZERO ledger rows with the private tier off; with it on they routed to network=private only; a public->private flip moved all 5 rows to 'unpinned' and the node kept the CIDs only because three other videos still referenced them (reference-count guard); a state change to 'quarantined' unpinned all 5 rows on the next sweep tick
SC1_mirror_and_playback.delete_defect: deleting a video left all 5 rows 'pinned' with video_id AND owner_user_id NULL — unreachable by every sweep branch, CIDs still on the node. Root cause: media_ipfs_pins.video_id is ON DELETE SET NULL and the delete hooks fire after the row is gone, so UnpinVideo lists by a video_id the FK already nulled. Fixed on vidra-core#218 and re-measured live: the next reconcile tick re-armed 10 orphan rows (two deleted videos' worth, including one orphaned before the fix) and the worker dropped the CID no live row still referenced.
SC1_mirror_and_playback.retranscode: TestIntegrationMirrorPinsPromotedGeneration passes against the real node; live, an admin HLS rerun promoted generation r2 and the worker re-added the tree at the new master_key prefix (files=14, 1066007 bytes). The r2 output was byte-identical to r1, so the CID did not move and the release-the-old half was not separable in the live run.

player_fallback.mechanism: client-side: the watch page probes the gateway master with fetch() and only switches hls.js when the probe is ok; a failed probe sets the 'error' state and playback continues from the server

image_fallback.measured: with the gateway stopped, GET /videos/{id}/thumbnail and /storyboard.jpg still answered 307 to the dead gateway (Cache-Control: public, max-age=300); following the redirect gave 'Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 8081' and 0 bytes. delivery.mirrorSource fails open on 'not pinned' and on a ledger error, but never on an unreachable gateway, and there is no runtime toggle to stop it without a restart.

qoe.server_half: PASS — a beacon carrying a gateway segment URL was classified delivery_source=ipfs-gateway
qoe.client_half: PARTIAL — playback.start fires once per session, so a viewer who switches to IPFS and watches to the end contributes one row labelled api-proxy; only a later rebuffer/bitrate_switch/error event carries the new source

admin_system.measured: GET /admin/system probes s3, smtp, search, ffmpeg, clamav, postgres, redis and settings_sync. There is no ipfs component, so an unreachable node never degrades that page. GET /api/v1/ipfs/status does report node_reachable=false, and it did.

kill_switch.semantics: IPFS_ENABLED=false is a restart-only env switch (no instancesettings key). With it off: no mirror worker starts, an upload produced ZERO ledger rows, GET /videos/{id} omits the ipfs object so the watch toggle is absent (confirmed in Chromium), the thumbnail route answers 200 from the api instead of redirecting, and GET /ipfs/status and POST /admin/ipfs/reconcile both answer 503 ipfs_disabled. EXISTING pins are LEFT ALONE — the ledger kept 15 private + 25 public 'pinned' rows and the node kept all 15 pins — so the switch stops publishing and advertising but never retracts. It governs the PUBLIC tier only; IPFS_MIRROR_PRIVATE is a separate switch and a private-only deployment is explicitly supported.

SC3_reconcile.dead_letter_rearm: PASS — a row staged state='failed', cid='' was re-armed to 'pending' by POST /admin/ipfs/reconcile and re-pinned with a real CID within one drain
SC3_reconcile.outage_ladder: PASS — with the node down a fresh upload's 5 rows went state='pending', attempts 1→2, next_attempt_at ~1 min out, last_error 'add+pin rpc failed' / 'directory add+pin rpc failed'; the node came back and all 5 pinned on the next attempt
SC3_reconcile.node_lost_a_cid: FAIL — `ipfs pin rm` by hand, then reconcile: the ledger still said 'pinned' and the node still did not have it. Reconcile re-arms dead-lettered rows and sweeps ineligible ones; it never compares the ledger to the node.
SC3_reconcile.stray_pin: FAIL — a CID added directly to the node and never in the ledger survived reconcile untouched
SC3_reconcile.concurrency: PASS — measured through a counting reverse proxy in front of the kubo RPC: IPFS_PIN_CONCURRENCY=1 gave max_concurrent_add=1 over 5 adds; =3 gave max_concurrent_add=3 over 5 adds
SC3_reconcile.backfill: POST /admin/ipfs/reconcile seeded 5 intents (one per class) for the video uploaded while the mirror was off, and all 5 pinned

SC4_isolation.eligibility: private and unlisted videos and their derivatives route to network='private' (Route treats unlisted as private for mirroring); a public->private flip transitions the rows across swarms
SC4_isolation.replication: P1 held the private original; P2 fetched and pinned it over the keyed swarm (52715 bytes, then 45691 bytes for a second video after a P2 outage)
SC4_isolation.outsider_refusal: `ipfs swarm connect` from the keyless node failed at 'failed to negotiate security protocol: context deadline exceeded'; `ipfs cat <private cid>` timed out at 45 s with no bytes; the shipped TestOutsideNodeCannotFetch also passes
SC4_isolation.api_absence: 11 payloads (owner and anonymous detail for the private and unlisted videos, public and authenticated feeds, channel videos, the ActivityPub representation, search, /me/videos and /ipfs/status) contain ZERO of the 9 private CIDs; the positive control — the public video's hls CID — appears twice in the same corpus
SC4_isolation.public_gateway: the public gateway answered 404 in 7 ms for a private CID, and the public node's pin list never contained it

SC5_outage.p1_down: GET /ipfs/status reported networks.private.node_reachable=false while networks.public stayed true; a private upload's 5 rows retried with the shipped ladder (attempts 1→2); public delivery was unaffected (thumbnail 307 to the gateway, HLS master 200); no crash
SC5_outage.p1_recovery: all 5 rows pinned on attempt 3, about 2 minutes after the node returned
SC5_outage.p2_down_and_back: P2 is a pull replica (no cluster configured), so its outage does not touch the ledger; after restart it reconnected to P1 and converged on the CID it had missed
SC5_outage.dm_no_pin: no code path anywhere in vidra-core enqueues ClassDMAttachment — the constant exists only so the eligibility table can assert the refusal — Route defaults to NetworkNone for it on BOTH swarms, and the lab ended with zero dm_attachment rows. A15 (MSG-03) already proved the invariant against a real kubo node.
SC5_outage.observability_gap: the mirror writes NO job_runs rows and carries no correlation id; its only durable trace is media_ipfs_pins (attempts, next_attempt_at, last_error) plus ipfs_pin_ok / ipfs_unpin_ok logs

SC6_wrong_actors.toggle: viewer-side only — the watch page's IPFS switch worked for an anonymous browser session and needs no privilege
